content.content:
1. Single commitment. The dependent records one commitment — a draft's record has registry-local identity and references, not graph/node identity. Read all of its clauses as one commitment and fail on any clause that could be decided, changed or dropped on its own without the remaining clauses changing: name the clause and the separate commitment it settles. A clause whose soundness rests on a prerequisite the dependent does not name in depends_on also fails this criterion: name the clause and the unnamed prerequisite.

2. Licence and named prerequisites. No element of the dependent contradicts a prerequisite the dependent names in depends_on; fail on every contradicting element, naming the element and the prerequisite it departs from. For each clause, identify the prerequisite whose decision the clause actually uses; fail if that prerequisite is not named in depends_on, naming the clause and the missing prerequisite. The prerequisites recorded here decide, among them: a node's id is the jj change id and appears in the filename and in edge targets, never in the document (xwyryumr); a node is the JSON document nodes/<id>.json carrying kind, content and its outgoing edges (kpovwvyw); what counts as a valid node is the schema (tksoxwpy); log lists the nodes with their edges and settles no filtering (zqkqvlyo); a draft names exactly one node and the edit it belongs to and is written in its own workspace (znskspqs); recording places the named file edits into the named node's change (rvyrosmp); draft state lives in one work-state registry under .deccy/work/ inside the state directory (ulqqklzk). A clause that legitimately uses a prerequisite outside this set is itself a finding for this criterion: name the clause and that prerequisite.
content.rationale: A licence-only check asks whether the dependent contradicts the prerequisites it happened to name. That is too weak for this use: the commitment is about what the record's identity and references are and are not, so a decision can avoid every contradiction with the named nodes and still split that into clauses that are decided, changed or dropped separately, or rest an unnamed clause on a node, draft or recording decision the dependent never drew an edge to. Criterion 1 tests that the commitment is atomic; criterion 2 tests contradiction against the named prerequisites and that each clause names the prerequisite its soundness actually rests on. The dependent is prose, so no artifact runs: a reviewer applies both criteria to the recorded nodes.
